description:
pkix-ct/src/verify.rs:504-529

```rust
pub fn verify_sth(&self, log_id: &[u8; 32], sth: &SignedTreeHead)
    -> Result<&CtLog>
```

The `log_id` argument is the SHA-256 of the log's SPKI DER. The
`SignedTreeHead` struct (lines 568-583) does NOT carry a `log_id`
field. The caller must source the log_id from somewhere else
(typically from the SCT they're verifying inclusion for, or from
the log's HTTPS endpoint metadata).

Contrast with `verify_sct_for_cert(&self, sct: &SCT, cert_der:
&[u8])`: the SCT carries `log_id` inline, so the caller doesn't have
to pass it separately.

Two problems:

1. Inconsistent contract: `verify_sct_*` is "look up log_id from the
   parsed object"; `verify_sth` is "caller, you bring the log_id".
   Callers writing wrapper code have to remember which is which.

2. Wire-format `TreeHeadSignature` (RFC 6962 §3.5) does NOT include
   `log_id` in the signed structure. That's a real constraint: the
   STH wire form doesn't carry log_id, so the caller MUST track it
   externally. But the API can still help — `SignedTreeHead` could
   carry a `log_id` field that the caller fills in at parse time
   (analogous to how the SCT struct's `log_id` is filled in by
   the SCT parser).

Recommendation: add `log_id: [u8; 32]` to `SignedTreeHead` (PKIX-ppbr.15
unblocks this with #[non_exhaustive]), and drop the separate
parameter from `verify_sth`:

```rust
pub fn verify_sth(&self, sth: &SignedTreeHead) -> Result<&CtLog> {
    let log = self.logs.get(&sth.log_id).ok_or(Error::UnknownLog)?;
    ...
}
```

The caller still has to source the log_id, but they store it in the
typed struct where it belongs, not as a parallel parameter.

Priority P3; this is a consistency/idiomatic-Rust issue more than a
correctness one.
title: verify_sth takes log_id separately even though typical caller has SCT with matching log_id
